full_judgment:
2. Opposite parties 1 and 2 brought the case for pre-emption within the statutory period of limitation on the ground that they are co-sharers 10 the case holding. The case land was transferred by the opposite party 3 to stranger opposite party 1 on 13.7.79 without serving notice to the petitioners under section 89 of the Act. As opposite party the present petitioner contested the pre-emption proceeding on the ground that the case was barred by limitation, Preemptors were not co-sharers and the case land being homestead is not agricultural in nature, the case is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties. Both the courts below found that the case was filed in time and that the preemptors were co-sharers and there was no defect of parties and also they have allowed preemption finding that the case land although described in the question deed as bhiti and homestead it is part of agricultural holding. 

 6. I have coddled the said decision and seen that the decision was made in respect of the homestead land falling within the Municipal area embracing within the ambit of Non-agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949. So, that decision has no application in the instant case.
